topic: Properties and Changes of Matter and Waste Management
key_concepts: Matter is anything that has mass and volume.
Porosity is a material property that allows water absorption.
Malleability allows materials like gold to be shaped.
Elasticity allows materials like rubber bands to stretch and return to shape.
Ductility allows materials like copper to be drawn into wires.
Metals are useful because they are hard and can be shaped.
Chlorofluorocarbons can deplete the ozone layer.
Physical changes do not change the composition of matter.
Chemical changes form new substances, as in rusting, burning, and souring.
Spoiled food can be identified by bubbles and foul odor.
Non-biodegradable wastes should be recycled or reused.
The 5Rs of waste management are reuse, reduce, recycle, repair, and recover.
